title: Fuel Conservation
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Cook nothing in this sub-strand without the teacher. A demonstration with two pots of water, one with a lid and one without, on the same jiko shows the saving clearly.

skills.key_step: The child names the fuels used at home (firewood, charcoal, paraffin, cooking gas, biogas, electricity), says which are solid, liquid or gas, and that petrol and diesel are for engines.

floor.question: Is paraffin a solid, a liquid or a gas?

representations: pictures of a jiko, a gas cylinder, a paraffin stove
a three-column table: solid, liquid, gas
a walk round the school kitchen
steps: Say what it is: solid, liquid or gas.
Say what it is used for at home.

board.do: Draw three boxes: solid, liquid, gas.
Write charcoal and firewood in Solid.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a fuel used for cooking at home?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what burns in a jiko, a gas cooker and a car. Talk about why petrol is dangerous indoors.

misconceptions.ask: Which list names only fuels used at home?
misconceptions.repair: Ask each learner which fuels their home uses and make one class list.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a liquid fuel?
misconceptions.repair: Pour paraffin, hold charcoal and ask how each can be carried and stored.

listen_for: Only things that burn with a flame
misconceptions.ask: Which of these is used for cooking in some homes?
misconceptions.repair: Show a picture of an electric cooker and ask what makes it hot.

checks.question: Name a gas fuel used for cooking.
Is petrol used for cooking at home?

skills.key_step: The child says how to save fuel when cooking: cover the pot, use dry firewood, soak hard foods, cut food small, put out the fire when done, use an energy-saving jiko and a fireless cooker.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the fuels used at home.
floor.question: Name a fuel used at home.

representations: two pots of water, one with a lid
steps: Prepare food so it cooks fast: soak, cut small.
Put the fire out when cooking is done.

board.do: Draw two pots on a jiko, one with a lid.
Write "lid on: heat stays in, less fuel".

listen_for: Cooking with the lid off so you can watch
misconceptions.ask: Which habit saves fuel when boiling beans?
misconceptions.repair: Boil two pots of water, one with a lid and one without, and time them.

listen_for: Add more wood so the flame is big
misconceptions.ask: The pot is boiling. What should the cook do to save fuel?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether the water gets hotter than boiling when the flame is bigger.

misconceptions.ask: Which firewood saves the most fuel?
misconceptions.repair: Try to light a dry stick and a wet one and compare smoke and heat.

misconceptions.ask: How can you use less fuel to cook dry beans?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a soaked and a dry bean: press both, then count how long each takes to cook in the demonstration.

checks.question: Why cover a pot when cooking?
checks.answer: heat stays in so it cooks faster with less fuel

checks.question: Why should firewood be dry?
checks.answer: it burns well and gives more heat
